_comment: Each arm implements evaluate(state, questions, config) -> Run. arm_config_id is recorded on every row; change the config, change the id, never reuse one. The enabled set is SUBSCRIPTION-ONLY by deliberate choice: no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is required to run this study. opus5/haiku45 remain defined but disabled -- they are the metered-API arms, and enabling them would turn the headline back into a model-vs-model comparison. See FINDINGS.md Appendix C.
_role_values: role is a documentation label; NOTHING branches on it (verified 2026-09-20). Permitted values: classifier_under_test | headline_baseline | secondary_baseline | mid_tier_baseline | high_tier_baseline | metered_api_baseline (DISABLED) | test_double. Do NOT use 'treatment' or 'control' here -- those belong to the routing A/B, which assigns a ROUTING ARM to a delegated task. This file describes CLASSIFIER ARMS. See CONTEXT.md.

opus5._comment: Do NOT set thinking:{type:'disabled'} on Opus 5 — documented failure mode where tool calls leak into visible text. Low effort is the correct lever ON THIS MODEL. It is not a general rule: `effort` is a 4.6+ control, and on a pre-4.6 model such as Haiku 4.5 it is inert. See cc_haiku45 and JEV-41.

haiku45._comment: The incumbent a reader would EXPECT: nobody deploys Opus as a hook gate, so an Opus-only comparison is a strawman informed readers will discount. Stated as an expectation and not as a measured fact, because our own data contradicts the premise that goes with it. Under `claude -p`, Haiku 4.5 was the SLOWEST and most token-hungry cc_* arm, not the cheapest — partly our misconfiguration (JEV-41, fixed) and partly Haiku 4.5's 4,096-token cache-read minimum (not fixable here). Whether Haiku is the cheap tier in this harness is a question this study answers, not an assumption it starts from.

cc_opus5._comment: Claude Code on the subscription, as it actually ships. This is the headline baseline. It bundles the model with a ~5.2K-token preamble, a tool round trip and a process spawn, so the study's claim is about Claude Code as deployed, NOT about Opus 5 as a classifier. The report decomposes harness overhead from model work so a reader can see exactly how much of any gap is attributable to which.

cc_haiku45._comment: As cc_opus5, on Haiku, EXCEPT for max_thinking_tokens -- see JEV-41. Haiku 4.5 is pre-4.6: it has no adaptive thinking and no output_config.effort, so Claude Code gives it a FIXED thinking budget and `effort: low` cannot lower it. Measured at v1: 741 median thinking tokens against 0 for cc_opus5 and cc_sonnet5 on identical state at the same effort. max_thinking_tokens: 0 maps to thinking:{type:'disabled'} and is the only lever that reaches a pre-4.6 model. `effort` is kept, and is INERT on this model -- it is recorded so the argv stays comparable with the other cc_* arms, not because it does anything here. arm_config_id bumped v1 -> v2 at this change: rows carrying cc-haiku45-cli-v1 are a different configuration and their cost and latency do not pool with v2's.
cc_haiku45._not_fixed: cache_read_input_tokens is 0 on every v1 call and stays 0 on v2 -- a SEPARATE defect from the thinking one, left unfixed ON PURPOSE. Haiku 4.5's minimum cacheable prefix is 4,096 tokens against 512 on Opus 5, so the stable system+tools breakpoint of this deliberately lean invocation silently creates no entry and the only entry that exists sits after the per-decision state. Distinct states never hit; the same state repeated DOES hit (0 -> 5,613), and padding the system prompt past 4,096 makes cross-state reads appear at once (12,744 read on two unrelated states, writes falling to ~1,735). It is therefore fixable here, by adding ~9K tokens of filler to a classifier prompt -- which would change what this arm measures. The arm measures Claude Code as it ships. The zero cache read is published as a finding about pre-4.6 models behind `claude -p`, not engineered away.

cc_sonnet5._comment: The middle routing tier, and the one that matters most for the economics: opus->sonnet captures 75% of the opus->haiku saving at a far smaller capability drop. Also a baseline arm in its own right -- if Sonnet classifies as well as Opus, the 'frontier model as reference' framing weakens.

sonnet5._comment: Metered-API twin of cc_sonnet5. Disabled with the other metered arms; needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

cc_fable51._comment: Fable 5.1. NOT a cheap tier -- at $10/$50 it is twice Opus on input and output. It earns a place because its cache reads are half Opus's in absolute terms, so on cache-heavy terse turns it is cheaper. That makes the routing ladder two-dimensional rather than a single cost axis.
